pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.intro: HivePulse is a hive record book for beekeepers. Up to ten colonies are free for good; the supporter subscription lifts that limit and unlocks what a larger beekeeping operation needs. One price, billed yearly, cancellable at any time.
pricing.q1title: What happens when I reach ten colonies?
pricing.q1body: Only adding the eleventh one stops. Nothing already recorded is hidden, locked or deleted — not an inspection, not a photo, not a hive. A limit that took away work somebody had already done would be the wrong thing to do to a record of living animals, so it never does.
pricing.q2title: What does it cost, and is tax included?
pricing.q2body: {price} a year for an account, including VAT where it applies. There is no monthly plan: beekeeping runs in seasons, and a monthly subscription would mostly bill people for the winter.
pricing.q3body: On the subscription page of your account, with no notice period. The subscription then runs to the end of the year you paid for and simply does not renew. Your colonies stay; only adding more than ten stops again.
pricing.q4title: Can I get my money back?
pricing.q4body: Yes. As a consumer in the European Union you have fourteen days to withdraw from an online purchase without giving a reason. The refund policy says who refunds it and how.
pricing.q5body: On this website, signed in to your account — the subscription belongs to the account and not to a device, so it counts on the website, on Android and on the iPhone at the same time. The apps do not sell it.
pricing.q6title: What stays free, whatever I do?
pricing.q6body: The Asian hornet tracker, the beekeeping year, QR codes, inspections recorded without a signal, the community map and the export of your own data. They are free on purpose, and not as a trial.
pricing.legal: The terms of use, the refund policy and the privacy policy apply to every purchase.

mission.title: One third of everything you eat depends on bees
mission.p1: Honey bees and wild pollinators fertilize roughly 35 % of the world's food supply — fruits, vegetables, nuts, and oils. But populations have been declining for decades, and science is still scrambling to understand exactly why.
mission.li1: Colony Collapse Disorder affects millions of hives every year
mission.li2: Varroa mite is the #1 threat to managed bee colonies globally
mission.li3: Pesticides, habitat loss, and climate change compound the pressure
mission.li4: Real-time beekeeper data is essential for early-warning systems
mission.callout: When you log an inspection in HivePulse, you're not just managing your hive — you're adding a data point to a global early-warning network for bee health.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: HivePulse is an open-source beekeeping app. This policy explains what data we collect, why we collect it, and the choices you have — including how you control whether your apiary appears on the public map.
privacy.s1body: When you register: your email address, chosen display name, and preferred language. When you use the app: apiary names and GPS coordinates (if you enter them), hive details, and inspection records you log. We do not collect device identifiers, advertising IDs, or precise location data without you explicitly entering coordinates in the app. If you set a region for the beekeeping year: the country and postal code you enter. The postal code is looked up once and only the resulting position is kept, never an address.
privacy.s2body: The public map shows anonymised apiary pins to help visualise global beekeeping activity. Participation is strictly opt-in. By default every apiary you create is private — it never appears on the map and is never exposed via the public API. You can enable 'Show on public map' per apiary in the app settings at any time and disable it again just as easily. When enabled, the pin shows your apiary name, GPS coordinates, and hive count. No user identity or inspection detail is ever shared publicly.
privacy.s3body: Your data is used solely to run the app (authentication, storing and displaying your records) and, only if you opt in, to show your apiary pin on the public map and contribute aggregate counts to the global statistics (total apiaries, hives, inspections). We do not sell, trade, or rent personal data. We do not use it for advertising.
privacy.s4body: Running HivePulse involves a few companies that process data on our behalf, under a data processing agreement in each case. Hosting and the website: Vercel. Database: Neon (servers in the EU). Password reset emails: Resend. Crash reports: Sentry (servers in the EU, see the next section). Push notifications, only if you switch reminders on: Google Firebase for Android devices and Apple for iPhones, which receive a device token and the text of the notification. Map tiles come from the OpenStreetMap Foundation, so your IP address reaches them when you open a map. Fonts and icons are served from our own servers, so no third party learns anything from them. Paying for the supporter subscription, only if you buy one: RevenueCat, which checks the purchase and tells our server about it, and Paddle, which handles the payment itself and is the seller of record for it — your payment details are entered at Paddle and never reach us, and all we store is which subscription is running, where it came from and when it ends. Buying through the App Store or Google Play instead means Apple or Google take the payment and we learn the same little from RevenueCat. Visitor statistics: Umami Cloud, which according to its operator uses no cookies, no advertising identifiers and does not store full IP addresses; it records page views, the referring site, the country and the type of device. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in knowing whether the site is used at all (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Looking up a postal code (and an address you enter for an apiary): the OpenStreetMap Foundation’s search service Nominatim, which receives only that postal code and country or that address and none of your account data.
privacy.s5body: When the app or the server hits an unexpected error, a report goes to Sentry so it can be fixed. It contains the place in the code, the version, and the kind of device. It deliberately contains none of your content: no inspection notes, no passwords, no email address, no IP address, no screenshots and no record of what you typed. A report identifies your account by its internal number only. Reports are stored in the EU and kept for 30 days. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in a working, secure application (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
privacy.s6body: For EU/EEA users, we process your data on the basis of contract performance (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) for the core app features, and on the basis of your explicit consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR) for public map participation. You can withdraw consent at any time by toggling the 'Show on public map' switch off. We operate from Switzerland, so the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP) applies to this processing as well; where the two differ, we follow whichever gives you the stronger right.
privacy.s7body: Your account data is kept for as long as your account is active. You can request full deletion by contacting us at the address below — we will delete your account and all associated records within 30 days. Anonymised aggregate statistics (total counts) that have already been served publicly cannot be retracted.
privacy.s8body: Under GDPR you have the right to access, rectify, erase, and port your personal data, and to object to processing. To exercise these rights, contact us at hivepulse@multihead.de. If you believe your rights have not been respected, you may lodge a complaint with your national data protection authority.
privacy.s9body: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt and never stored in plain text. API access requires a signed JWT token. Data in transit is encrypted via TLS. We review security practices regularly.
privacy.s10body: Questions about this policy or your data? Write to hivepulse@multihead.de. The controller is Benjamin Müller, Sonnhaldenweg 5D, 4450 Sissach, Switzerland.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: HivePulse is a beekeeping application for the web, Android and iPhone. These terms describe what you can expect from it and what it expects from you. They are written to be read, not to be skipped.
terms.s1body: They cover the HivePulse website, the Android app and the iPhone app, including the free account and the supporter subscription. Two separate documents cover the rest: the privacy policy says what happens to your data, and the refund policy says how money comes back. HivePulse is operated by {operator}; the full details are in the imprint.
terms.s2body: You need an account to record colonies and inspections. Keep your password to yourself; anything done with your account is treated as done by you. One person, one account: to work on an apiary together, invite the other person rather than sharing a login. You can delete your account at any time and your data goes with it. The deletion page says exactly what disappears and what a running subscription means for it.
terms.s3body: Up to 10 colonies, and inspection statistics covering the past 365 days. Everything else is free and stays free: the hornet tracker, the community map, QR codes for your hives, the export of your own data, and both apps. Reaching a limit never closes what already exists. If you are above 10 colonies when a subscription ends, they remain and stay editable; you simply cannot add new ones until you are below the limit again.
terms.s4body: 19.99 € per year, renewing yearly until you cancel. It raises the colony limit, opens the regional health map and unlocks the treatment record. The price is shown before you buy and includes the tax of your country. A year rather than a month because beekeeping is seasonal: almost everything happens between March and October. You can cancel at any time and keep the subscription until the period you have paid for runs out.
terms.s5body: On the website the seller is Paddle, as merchant of record: the contract of sale is between you and Paddle, they take the payment, issue the invoice and remit the VAT. Their terms govern the purchase itself; these terms govern your use of HivePulse. In the iPhone app the seller is Apple, in the Android app it is Google, and their terms apply in the same way. Whichever route you take, the subscription unlocks the same features on every device you sign in on, because it belongs to your account and not to the device.
terms.s6body: Your apiaries, colonies, inspections and photographs belong to you. They are not sold and not handed to advertisers. You can export them at any time and take them elsewhere. Something becomes publicly visible only where you chose it: a hornet catch on the public map, an apiary you marked as visible, a photograph you submitted to the community. The privacy policy is the detailed version of this paragraph.
terms.s7body: Use it for beekeeping. Do not enter other people's accounts, do not hammer the site with automated requests beyond ordinary use, do not upload anything unlawful, and do not report hornet findings you have invented, because other beekeepers act on them. The source code is open and you may run your own copy; that permission comes from the licence in the repository, not from this page. An account used to harm others can be closed.
terms.s8title: 8. What is promised, and what is not
terms.s8body: HivePulse is run by one person, with care and without a guarantee of availability. It can be unreachable, a feature can carry a bug, and data you never exported can be lost — so keep your own copy of anything you cannot afford to lose. Liability is unlimited for intent, for gross negligence and for injury to life, body or health, and otherwise limited to what the law requires. The application supports your record keeping; it does not replace a beekeeper's legal obligations, and the treatment record remains a document you are responsible for.
terms.s9title: 9. Changes, ending, and which law applies
terms.s9body: These terms can change when the application changes or the law requires it. A change that affects you is announced in the app and on the news page before it takes effect, and no change to the subscription applies to a period you have already paid for. You end the agreement by deleting your account. HivePulse is operated from Switzerland, Swiss law applies and the place of jurisdiction is Sissach; if you are a consumer, that does not take away the mandatory protection of the law of the country you live in. For a purchase made on the website the seller is Paddle, so their terms govern the sale itself, including how a dispute about it is settled.

refunds.title: Refund Policy
refunds.intro: A subscription that turns out not to be what you hoped for should not need an argument. This page says how you get your money back, from whom, and what happens to your access afterwards.
refunds.s1body: Within 14 days of buying, ask and you get your money back. After that a subscription runs to the end of the period you paid for and then stops, if you cancelled it. A refund never deletes anything you recorded: your apiaries, colonies and inspections stay where they are.
refunds.s2body: As a consumer in the European Union you have a 14-day right of withdrawal on anything bought online, and you need no reason for it. It applies to the supporter subscription bought on this website. One thing is worth knowing: by asking for the features to be unlocked straight away you agree that the service starts before the 14 days are over, and the seller may keep the share matching the days you have already used. On a yearly subscription cancelled within the first fortnight that share is a few cents, and in practice the full amount is returned.
refunds.s3body: Bought on the website: your purchase confirmation comes from Paddle and carries a link to their customer portal, where you can request the refund directly. That is the fastest route, because Paddle holds the money and we do not. You can also write to hivepulse@multihead.de and we will pass the request on. Paddle refunds to the means of payment you used; how long it then takes is up to your bank, usually a few working days.
refunds.s4body: A refund ends the subscription at once, not at the end of the period — the money came back, so the features go back too. From that moment the colony limit applies again. Colonies above the limit are not deleted and nothing you recorded is touched; you simply cannot add new ones until you are below the limit or subscribe again. A treatment record you have already downloaded stays yours.
refunds.s5title: 5. Bought in the App Store or on Google Play
refunds.s5body: Then Apple or Google is the seller, not Paddle, and neither we nor Paddle can refund it. For Apple, report the problem at reportaproblem.apple.com. For Google, use the order history at play.google.com/store/account/orderhistory. Both have their own rules and their own deadlines, which can be more generous than the 14 days above. When their refund reaches our server, the access ends in the way section 4 describes.
refunds.s6title: 6. Cancelling is not the same as a refund
refunds.s6body: Cancelling stops the next renewal and leaves you the time you have paid for. That is usually what you want once the subscription has run a while: you keep everything until the year is up and nothing is charged again. Do it on the subscription page in your account, or wherever you bought it. Cancelling on the last day costs nothing extra; there is no notice period.

health.title: Data Health
health.crashDesc: Sends a deliberate error to the crash reporter, so you can see whether reports really arrive instead of finding out during a real failure.
health.crashSent: Sent as event {id} in environment {environment}. It should appear in Sentry within a minute — resolve it there afterwards.
health.crashOff: No crash reporter is configured, so nothing was sent.
health.crashFailed: The test could not be run.
health.crashDiagnosis: Technical detail: the key has {settingsChars} characters in the configuration and {envChars} in the process environment. Two zeros mean the hosting platform never passed it to the server.
health.defaultSigningKey: Warning: this server signs logins with the public default key from the source code. Anyone who knows it can forge a token for any account. Set a real SECRET_KEY in the hosting environment.
health.pushAndroidMissing: Android push is not configured: reminders never reach an Android phone. Needs FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID and FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON in the hosting environment.
health.pushIosMissing: iPhone push is not configured: reminders never reach an iPhone. Needs APNS_KEY_ID, APNS_TEAM_ID and APNS_PRIVATE_KEY_P8 in the hosting environment.
health.paddleKeyExpiring: The Paddle API key expires in {days} day(s). When it does, RevenueCat can no longer reach Paddle and web purchases fail, while this server keeps answering as if nothing were wrong. Rotate it in Paddle, paste it into RevenueCat, and move PADDLE_API_KEY_EXPIRES_AT with it.
health.paddleKeyExpired: The Paddle API key expired {days} day(s) ago. RevenueCat cannot reach Paddle, so every web purchase is failing — nothing else here would say so.
health.paddleKeyUnknown: Nobody wrote down when the Paddle API key expires. The live account does not allow a key without an expiry date, so there is one; set PADDLE_API_KEY_EXPIRES_AT to it (YYYY-MM-DD).

deleteAccount.title: Deleting your account and data
deleteAccount.intro: You can delete your HivePulse account yourself, at any time, without asking anyone. This page explains how and what exactly disappears — it exists because Google and Apple require it to be readable without installing the app.
deleteAccount.inAppTitle: In the app or on the website
deleteAccount.step1: Open your profile: in the apps under Settings, on the website under Dashboard → Profile.
deleteAccount.step2: Scroll to the bottom and choose “Delete account”.
deleteAccount.step3: Confirm. There is no waiting period and no further email.
deleteAccount.immediate: The deletion happens immediately and cannot be undone. Export your inspections first if you want to keep them — the dashboard offers a CSV download per apiary.
deleteAccount.removed1: Your account: email address, name, language and password.
deleteAccount.removed2: All your apiaries and hives, including their QR codes.
deleteAccount.removed3: Every inspection you recorded, with notes and custom fields.
deleteAccount.removed4: Your sessions and, if you enabled reminders, the device token used to send them.
deleteAccount.keptBody: Hornet reports and hornet traps stay. They are observations about the environment that other beekeepers rely on, and they are not linked to your account afterwards — the trap keeps its name and location, but no longer points at a person. Aggregate community statistics also stay, because they contain no personal data: a number of hives per region, never a hive of yours.
deleteAccount.retentionBody: In the live database the deletion is immediate — nothing of your account is left a minute later. Our hosting provider keeps automatic database backups for up to 30 days; a backup can only ever be restored as a whole, never for a single account, and after that window the data is gone from there too. The hornet reports and traps described above have no retention limit, because they no longer relate to a person. We keep no separate copies, no archives and no exports.
deleteAccount.noAccessBody: If you cannot log in any more, write to us and we will delete the account for you within 30 days. Use the address the account was registered with, so we can tell whose account it is:
deleteAccount.subTitle: If you have a subscription, cancel it first
deleteAccount.subBody: Deleting your HivePulse account does not cancel a subscription. A subscription bought in the App Store or on Google Play belongs to that store account, and one bought on this website belongs to the payment provider — HivePulse cannot cancel any of them for you. Cancel it before you delete the account, or you will keep being charged for something you can no longer reach.
deleteAccount.subWhere: In the App Store: Settings → your name → Subscriptions. On Google Play: Payments and subscriptions. On the website: the link on the Subscription page in your dashboard.

beta.title: Try HivePulse before everybody else
beta.intro: HivePulse is finished, but not yet in the stores. Before Google lets a new developer publish an app, twelve people have to test it for two weeks — so this phase is not a formality, it is the gate. If you keep bees and own a phone, you can help.
beta.notOpenYet: The test rounds are being set up and the links will appear here. Write to us and you will get them the moment they exist.
beta.joinNote: To take part you need a Google account for Android or an Apple ID for the iPhone — the same one your phone already uses. Inside the app you then create a HivePulse account with an email address and a password; it takes a minute and costs nothing. You can leave at any time.
beta.expect1: Install the app and set up one apiary with a couple of hives. Fifteen minutes.
beta.expect2: Record a visit the next time you are at the hives — that is the part worth testing in the field, gloves and all.
beta.expect3: Stay in the test for two weeks. Google counts the testers daily, so leaving early sets the clock back for everyone.
beta.expect4: Tell us what was confusing. One sentence is more useful than none, and “nothing broke” is also an answer.
beta.feedbackBody: No forum, no account, no ticket system — just write to
beta.feedbackHint: Useful in a report: which phone, what you did, what you expected instead. A photo of the screen says more than a description. If the app closed itself, it has already sent a crash report — you do not have to describe it.
beta.dataBody: The same as for everybody else: your apiaries are private unless you put them on the public map yourself, nothing is sold or passed on, and there is no advertising. Test builds carry crash reporting, which sends the place in the code and the kind of device — never your notes, your password or your address. You can delete your account and everything in it yourself at any time.
beta.androidNote: On Android, Google only lets in accounts we have registered beforehand — without an entry the link says “App not available”. So send us your Google account address first, with the form below.
beta.androidNoteSubject: HivePulse Android test: please add me
beta.formLead: One field is enough. It sends us a message and stores nothing — no account, and no list you have to get yourself off again later.
beta.formEmailHint: The Google account your phone already uses, or your Apple ID for the iPhone. We need it only to put you on the tester list.
beta.formSent: Thank you — that reached us. You will hear from us once the account is on the list; the install link works from then on.
beta.formError: The message could not be sent. Please write to us directly instead.

survey.title: Does the beekeeping year fit where you are?
survey.subtitle: A quarter of an hour of your experience, and the calendar gets better for every beekeeper in your region. No account needed.
survey.why: The 38 entries of the beekeeping year were written once, for central Germany, and moved elsewhere by a formula: so many days later per degree of latitude, so many per 100 metres of altitude. That formula is an estimate. Nobody has checked it against what beekeepers actually do in Andalusia, in Brittany or in Masuria — and the people who can check it are the people who keep bees there.
survey.whyNothingChanges: Nothing you send changes a date by itself. Ratings from the same region are grouped, and only when at least five beekeepers within 150 km agree does the median correction reach somebody who knows the region and can approve it.
survey.placeLead: First, where do you keep your bees? The dates you rate are then the dates you would actually see — not the ones written for central Germany.
survey.privacy: Stored are the country, your position rounded to about 11 km, and your ratings. The postal code is looked up once and then dropped. No name, no address, no link to an account.
survey.loadFailed: The timeline could not be loaded. Please try again.
survey.notLocated: That postal code could not be found, so the dates below are the unshifted ones. You can still rate them, but a correction needs a place — please check the code before sending.
survey.shifted: The dates below are moved {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} against central Germany, for your place.
survey.rateLead: Rate only what you have an opinion about — everything you leave alone is simply not sent. Tap an answer again to take it back.
survey.nothingRated: Nothing is rated yet. Pick an answer for at least one entry.
survey.sendFailed: The ratings could not be sent. Please try again.
survey.doneBody: {accepted, plural, one {# rating arrived.} other {# ratings arrived.}}
survey.doneReplaced: {replaced, plural, one {One of them replaced what this browser had said before.} other {# of them replaced what this browser had said before.}}
survey.doneNext: Nothing has changed yet. Once five beekeepers near you agree, the correction goes to someone who can approve it.
